clue.text: Details of problem suggest reducing staff as solution

definitions.text: Details of problem suggest reducing staff as solution

parts.words: Details of problem suggest reducing staff as solution
parts.note: read as a business case: the hard data about a company's trouble point to cutting jobs as the remedy, and that data is the phrase wanted

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means hard statistics and data, the detailed information about any situation.

clue.text: Foreign money given to one's boy

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and remains that of Switzerland
one's is a contraction of one is, I IS, giving I plus S

explanation.surface: A father hands foreign cash to his son.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, a common male forename.

clue.text: After tea, I run to seat

indicators.note: the following letters are placed after the word for tea in the answer

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their tea and hurries to sit down.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat with a back for one person is the piece of furniture in question.

clue.text: Rigorous training here makes army officers pass out

definitions.text: Rigorous training here makes army officers pass out

parts.words: Rigorous training here makes army officers pass out
parts.note: pass out seems to mean faint from exhaustion, but it is the military term for graduating from an academy

explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst in Berkshire is where British Army officer cadets train and graduate.

clue.text: Unaffected by direction to cancel flat

definitions.meaning: in music notation a sign that cancels a previous flat or sharp

explanation.surface: A tenant shrugs off instructions to give up their flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural behaviour is genuine and unpretentious; in music the natural sign restores a note after a flat.

clue.text: Strongly confirm, with most weight

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud or strong
attest means confirm or bear witness to

explanation.surface: Someone strongly vouches for the heaviest contestant.
explanation.definitionFit: The heaviest, carrying the greatest bulk, is the superlative of fat.

clue.text: Man's speaking appearance

indicators.note: speaking signals that the word for man's is said aloud to give a different spelling

parts.note: guy's, a man's, sounds the same as the plural guys

explanation.surface: How a man talks shapes how he comes across.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is an outward appearance or semblance, often a false one.

clue.text: Getting down details-one may have it taped

definitions.meaning: writing information down, keeping a record of facts
a tape or disc capturing sound, as in a taped music track

explanation.surface: A clerk noting the facts while a tape machine captures it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a record of facts is one sense; the other is a captured piece of sound kept on tape.

clue.text: Fine weather report-shade needed

definitions.meaning: a forecaster describing a cloudless day might simply say the heavens are clear
a shade is a tint or hue of colour

explanation.surface: A forecast of sunshine, though some shade will be wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear sky's colour on a sunny day is also the name of a pale azure hue.

clue.text: Opposed to profit, in a way

indicators.note: in signals that the word for profit is placed inside the letters for a way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Someone objects to making money from something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is being in opposition to it.

clue.text: In outskirts of Tewkesbury, wise woman is nervous

indicators.note: In signals that the woman's word is put inside the letters taken from the town name
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a wise woman is an old term for a witch

explanation.surface: A village herbalist on the edge of a Gloucestershire town is jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' takes T and Y, the first and last letters of Tewkesbury, a town in Gloucestershire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitchy describes someone jittery and on edge, showing anxiety.

clue.text: Animal proverbially getting things back to front?

definitions.text: Animal proverbially getting things back to front?

parts.words: Animal proverbially getting things back to front?
parts.note: the proverb about putting the cart before the beast that pulls it describes doing things in the wrong order

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy draught horse pulls a cart; the saying about the cart going first is about reversed order.

clue.text: Flynn seen in character role

indicators.note: seen in signals that the name lies within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A film star appears in a character part.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across chaRACTER ROLe: the last two letters of character plus the first three of role.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol Flynn was the Hollywood actor famed for swashbuckling roles.

clue.text: More than one reveals problems

indicators.note: problems suggests the letters of the next word are in trouble and rearranged

explanation.surface: An investigation uncovers more than one difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Several means a few, a number greater than two.

clue.text: Not impressed with organ piece

definitions.meaning: impressed in the sense of forced into service, as press gangs did; not compelled means freely done
a solo played on a church organ before or after a service

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by a church organ recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Done of one's own free will rather than compelled; also an organ solo at a church service.

clue.text: I let cat out — so touching

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Releasing the cat is a heartwarming moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch, perceptible by feel.

clue.text: Dairy product parliamentarian fed to pet

indicators.note: fed to signals that the politician is placed inside the word for a pet, as food goes into an animal

parts.note: a cat is a household pet
a Member of Parliament is a parliamentarian

explanation.surface: A dairy treat is given by an MP to their pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese made from cow's milk.

clue.text: Recounts taxes once squeezed the Spanish

indicators.note: squeezed signals that the taxes word holds the Spanish article tightly inside it

parts.note: rates were the former British local property taxes
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone tells how tax demands once crushed the Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to narrate or tell it.

clue.text: Nuclear plant creator redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters of creator are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: An atomic power station whose designer has reworked it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor is the core apparatus of an atomic power station.

clue.text: Quickly look at boy, upset by disgrace

parts.note: to scan is to glance over quickly

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the word for boy upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: lad means boy

explanation.surface: A glance at a boy reveals he is upset by some shame.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is a public disgrace, an outrage causing shame.

clue.text: Hero finds Miss Moore a divine being

parts.note: Demi Moore is an American film actress
a god is a divine being

explanation.surface: A fan regards the actress Demi Moore as a goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a hero was often half-god, born of a deity and a mortal.

clue.text: Command to speak to recorder

definitions.meaning: to command is to order with authority
to speak words for a machine or secretary to take down

explanation.surface: A boss orders a secretary to take down a letter on tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to give orders; it also means to say words aloud for someone to write down.

clue.text: Well-ventilated cage in battery

parts.note: a well-aired place is dry rather than damp
a cell is a cage-like enclosure for a prisoner

explanation.surface: An airy cage installed inside a battery of hens.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry cell is a type of electric battery with a paste electrolyte.

clue.text: Upset to miss start of public address

indicators.note: to miss the start means the first letter of the following word is dropped

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name used for a public address system

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at missing the start of a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: TANNOY is the British trade name used generically for a loudspeaker system in stations and schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To annoy is to irritate or vex someone.

clue.text: Peasant left to carry symbol of servitude

parts.note: a yoke, worn by draught oxen, is a symbol of subjugation

explanation.surface: A farm labourer is left carrying the yoke of his bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: A yokel is an unsophisticated country dweller, a rustic.

clue.text: Go with Bill to business

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a company is a business

explanation.surface: A man named Bill accompanies someone to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To accompany is to escort or travel alongside someone.

clue.text: Smell of a foreign capital

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: The scent of an overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell or fragrance.

clue.text: Followed and changed direction, keeping right

indicators.note: keeping signals that the word for changed direction holds the letter for right inside it

parts.note: a sailing boat that tacks changes direction into the wind

explanation.surface: A yacht pursued another and changed course while staying to starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow their trail.

clue.text: Intimidating, or sounding so to me

indicators.note: sounding signals that the little word or is said aloud as a homophone

parts.note: in non-rhotic British speech or sounds like awe

explanation.surface: Something seems daunting, or at least it sounds that way to me.
explanation.walkthrough: In southern British English, 'or' and 'awe' are pronounced the same; SO and ME are taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome means inspiring awe or dread, overwhelming.

clue.text: London venue-called for one close to Victoria

definitions.text: London venue-called for one close to Victoria

parts.words: London venue-called for one close to Victoria
parts.note: a concert hall in Kensington named after Queen Victoria's husband, the prince consort, who was close to her

explanation.definitionFit: The famous domed concert hall in Kensington was named in memory of Prince Albert, Victoria's consort.
